In 2008, one phone company was worth more than eighty billion dollars. A president fought his own security team to keep its phone. The story begins in Waterloo, Canada, in 1984. Two engineering students start a company with a strange name: Research In Motion. Then, in 1999, they launch a small device with a full keyboard that does one magical thing. It pushes your email to you, wherever you are. Bankers buy it. Lawyers buy it. Politicians buy it. It's so addictive that people start calling it the CrackBerry. Then comes its most famous user. In 2008, Barack Obama campaigns with a BlackBerry glued to his hand. When he wins, his security team says no. Obama pushes back, and he keeps it. And BlackBerry had a secret weapon: BBM. By June 2008, the company is worth more than eighty billion dollars. It is the king of the keyboard. But one new phone was about to change everything. Follow for part two.
